analysis:
- Q2 revenue from operations was Rs 14,687 crore, up 21% YoY, with EBITDA up 8% to Rs 1,968 crore (13.4% margin, up 10 bps QoQ) and PAT up 5% to Rs 1,456 crore. Consolidated PAT rose 41% to Rs 1,861 crore, including a Rs 397 crore one-time gain. Wholesale volume grew 10.5%, with ICE up 8.4% and EV up 98%. Operating cash flow was Rs 2,159 crore.
- Hero gained Vahan market share in every month of the quarter, with ICE retail up 24% YoY and ICE scooter dispatches up 34%. Scooter capacity is now about 80,000 units a month. VIDA retail grew 105% (Vahan basis) and market share is near 13.5-14% in October. VIDA turned gross margin positive ahead of guidance, and its EBITDA drag fell to Rs 168 crore from Rs 232 crore in Q1. PLI covers nearly 100% of the portfolio from October, which should translate to roughly 13% of EV revenue from Q3.
- VIDA capacity reached 30,000 units a month in September, with a plan for 45,000 by Q4 and over 80,000 by Q2 of next fiscal. Dealer stock is about one day. Full-year capex guidance is Rs 1,500 crore, with about Rs 600 crore spent in H1. A Rs 700 crore Global Parts Center 2.0 is expected to be fully operational by the end of next calendar year.
- Commodity inflation was about 1% QoQ in Q2, and about 5.5% across Q1 and Q2, of which roughly half was recovered through pricing. A price increase of about Rs 1,000 per unit was taken on October 1. Management expects mild input cost pressure in Q3, but margins to remain broadly stable. The medium-term EBITDA margin target is 14-16%, expected over the next few quarters as commodities normalize. Management said growth investments will not be cut.
- Exports were hurt by an earthquake in Colombia (about 25% of exports) and a demand slowdown in Bangladesh, though export retail grew 19%. Management expects double-digit export growth in Q3 and Q4. Festival-to-date growth is 24%, with no share erosion, and rural demand is as good as or better than urban. The industry is expected to grow mid-to-high single digits in H2 and during the festive period. Three to four premium launches are planned for the rest of the fiscal year, and about 15,000 flex-fuel bikes have been dispatched in about two months.
